answer: Each identity stewards one juniper grove and locks an 80-credit bond. It buys tagged seedlings for a nursery fee, and an ivory tag binds each stem to that grove and its key. After a gale, auditors recount live stems against the public grove board and burn the bond if fewer than 90% survive. The k-th grove fee rises to 25+6(k-1) credits, so the 1,000th costs 6,019 and 1,000 fakes pay 3,022,000 in fees plus 80,000 locked. A rented-grove ring fails because one tagged stem cannot prove two groves. An honest steward pays 25 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
